sentences.en: Agave was foaming at the mouth.
sentences.zh: 阿伽沃当时口吐白沫。

sentences.en: Her rolling eyes were wild.
sentences.zh: 她双眼翻白，神情狂乱。

sentences.en: She was not in her right mind, but possessed by Bacchus, and she paid no heed to Pentheus.
sentences.zh: 她神志不清，被狄奥尼索斯附身，根本不把彭透斯放在眼里。

sentences.en: She grasped his left arm between wrist and elbow, set her foot against his ribs, and tore his arm off by the shoulder.
sentences.zh: 她一把抓住彭透斯的左臂（手腕和手肘之间），将脚抵在他的肋骨上，硬生生地把他的胳膊从肩膀处扯了下来。

sentences.en: It was no strength of hers that did it, but the god filled her and made it easy.
sentences.zh: 这不是她自己的力气，而是神明充满了她，让这一切变得轻而易举。

sentences.en: On the other side, Aino was at him, tearing at his flesh, and now Autinoe joined them, and the whole maniacal horde.
sentences.zh: 另一边，伊诺扑向了他，撕扯着他的血肉，接着奥托诺伊也加入了他们，还有整个疯狂的狂欢大军。

sentences.en: A single and continuous yell arose, Pentheus shrieking as long as life was left in him, the women howling in triumph.
sentences.zh: 现场爆发出一声连绵不断的惨叫，彭透斯只要还有一口气就在发出尖叫，女人们则狂喜地嚎叫着。

sentences.en: One of them carried off an arm, another a foot, the boots still laced on it.
sentences.zh: 她们中有人带走了一条胳膊，有人带走了一只脚，脚上还系着靴子。

sentences.en: The ribs were stripped, clawed clean, and women's hands, thick red with blood, were tossing, catching like a plaything Pentheus's flesh.
sentences.zh: 肋骨被剥得干干净净，血迹斑斑的女人们双手挥舞着，像玩耍玩具一样抛接彭透斯的血肉。

sentences.en: So that is the devastating climax of the most shocking, the most blood-soaked and notorious of all Greek tragedies, the Bacchae, by the great Athenian dramatist Euripides.
sentences.zh: 这就是希腊悲剧中最震撼、最血腥、最著名的作品——古雅典剧作家欧里庇得斯的《巴克科斯女祭司》那毁灭性的高潮。

sentences.en: It's a terrible scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其可怕的场景。

sentences.en: Pentheus is being ripped into pieces by these women possessed with the spirit of Bacchus,
sentences.zh: 彭透斯被这些被狄奥尼索斯精神附体的女人们撕成了碎片，

sentences.en: as he describes it, and the little bits of his flesh are left scattered under rocks and over trees.
sentences.zh: 正如他所描述的那样，他身上的血肉碎块散落在一块块岩石下和树木间。

sentences.en: Tom, you chose this lovely reading to begin the episode.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你选择这篇精彩的朗读来开启这一集。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: It's unbelievably dramatic.
sentences.zh: 这戏剧性简直难以置信。

sentences.en: It reads like a description from The Walking Dead or 28 Days
sentences.zh: 读起来就像《行尸走肉》或者《惊变28天》里的描写，

sentences.en: Later.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿。

sentences.en: It has a kind of real zombie vibe.
sentences.zh: 有一种真正的僵尸氛围。

sentences.en: And the scene where this is happening is Mount Kithoron, which is the very same mountain range south of Thebes in central Greece, where the infant
sentences.zh: 发生这一幕的地点是基斯托戎山，也就是希腊中部底比斯南部的同一座山脉，在上一集我们谈到过的索福克勒斯的戏剧中，还是婴儿的

sentences.en: Oedipus in Sophocles' play, which we talked about in the previous episode, was taken from his parents' palace.
sentences.zh: 俄狄浦斯就是从那里被带离他父母的宫殿的。

sentences.en: So generally, it's a place where terrible things happen.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，这是一个经常发生可怕事情的地方。

sentences.en: But the action in this play, in the Bacchae, with this poor man being torn to pieces, is set four generations before the time of Oedipus.
sentences.zh: 但这部戏《巴克科斯女祭司》中的情节，也就是这个可怜人被撕成碎片的场景，发生在俄狄浦斯时代之前整整四代人。

sentences.en: So Pentheus, the guy who's being torn to pieces, he was the grandfather of Jocasta, who was Oedipus' mother stroke wife.
sentences.zh: 所以被撕成碎片的彭透斯，其实是伊俄卡斯她的外祖父，而伊俄卡斯塔就是俄狄浦斯的母亲兼妻子。

sentences.en: And he ruled as Oedipus was going to rule in due course as the king of Thebes.
sentences.zh: 他统治底比斯的时候，正是俄狄浦斯后来将要统治的时间。

sentences.en: And we highlighted in the previous episode how the Theban royal family is the most dysfunctional dynasty in the whole of Greek myth.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集里强调过，底比斯王室是整个希腊神话中最不正常的王朝。

sentences.en: And this episode absolutely sets the seal on this reputation.
sentences.zh: 而这一集彻底坐实了这一名声。

sentences.en: Because Agave, who you described ripping off Pentheus' left arm, is Pentheus' mother.
sentences.zh: 因为你刚才形容徒手扯下彭透斯左臂的阿伽沃，正是彭透斯的亲生母亲。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And Aino and Otonawe, who are joining in the fun, are his aunts.
sentences.zh: 而加入这场狂欢的伊诺和奥托纳维，则是他的亲阿姨。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, as family rendezvous go, picnics up on the mountain, this is a very, very bad one.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，就家庭聚会或者山顶野餐而言，这真的是一次非常非常糟糕的聚会。

sentences.en: And what's going on here is not that they are, you know, you used the Walking Dead parallel.
sentences.zh: 这里发生的事情并不是——你刚才用了《行尸走肉》的类比——

sentences.en: They're not zombies.
sentences.zh: 她们并不是僵尸。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Although in a kind of way they are, they have become possessed, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 尽管某种程度上她们确实是，她们被附身了，对吧？

sentences.en: They've become ravers, I see in your notes.
sentences.zh: 我在你的笔记里看到，她们变成了狂欢者。

sentences.en: So what's that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Mynads.
sentences.zh: 迈纳德斯女祭司。

sentences.en: Mynads, yes.
sentences.zh: 迈纳德斯女祭司，是的。

sentences.en: So they've become what the Greeks called mynads, literally ravers.
sentences.zh: 所以她们成了希腊人所说的迈纳德斯，字面意思就是狂欢者。

sentences.en: And they have been gripped by a frenzy that in Greek was called a bakaya.
sentences.zh: 她们被一种疯狂所攫取，在希腊语中被称为“巴凯亚”。

sentences.en: And when you join a bakaya, if you're a mynad, you dress up in the skins of fawns or leopards and you roam the uplands,
sentences.zh: 当你加入巴凯亚时，如果你是一个迈纳德斯，你就会穿上小鹿或豹子的皮毛，在山地间游荡，

sentences.en: you know, you leave the kind of the plains, centers of civilization and go up into the hills.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你离开平原和文明的中心，走到群山之中。

sentences.en: And up there, you either, you suckle wild animals.
sentences.zh: 在那里，你要么用母乳喂养野生动物，

sentences.en: So you put them to your breast or you tear them to pieces with your bare hands.
sentences.zh: 把它们抱在胸前，要么就用赤手空拳把它们撕成碎片。

sentences.en: And this is a rite of kind of ecstatic dismemberment called spragmos in Greek.
sentences.zh: 这是一种被称为狂喜式肢解的仪式，在希腊语中叫作斯普拉格莫斯。

sentences.en: And if you are a mynad who is particularly off her face, then you might go one step further and eat, tear the flesh off your victim and eat it raw, which again, the Greeks
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个彻底陷入狂乱的迈纳德斯，你可能会更进一步，吃掉受害者，把受害者的肉从身上撕下来生吃，希腊人

sentences.en: called omophagia.
sentences.zh: 称之为生食仪式。

sentences.en: And the excitement of it is that you are subverting every norm that governs conventional society in Greece.
sentences.zh: 这种狂热的刺激在于，你在颠覆希腊传统社会的一切常规准则。

sentences.en: So you are abandoning your city for the uplands, for the wilds, you're human, but you're turning into a wild beaSt. And if you're a woman, then you are casting off all
sentences.zh: 所以你为了高地和荒野而抛弃了城市，你是人，却正在变成一头野兽；如果你是个女人，你就会抛弃所有

sentences.en: the kind of the rules, the assumptions, the decorum that are supposed to govern your behavior.
sentences.zh: 那些本该规范你行为的规则、假设和礼仪。

sentences.en: And in the Bacchae, Euripides describes the mynad's turning men to flight.
sentences.zh: 在《巴克科斯女祭司》中，欧里庇得斯描述了迈纳德斯女祭司把男人吓得落荒而逃的场景。

sentences.en: So men are playing the role of women.
sentences.zh: 所以男人在扮演女人的角色。

sentences.en: It's subverting gender norms, as critics would say now.
sentences.zh: 用评论家现在的话说，这是在颠覆性别规范。

sentences.en: We love doing that and the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 我们很喜欢这样做，剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: And this is what the bakaya is all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是“巴凯亚”的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: But having said that, it's not just mynad's.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这不仅仅是迈纳德斯女祭司们的专利。

sentences.en: Who are doing it.
sentences.zh: 她们在这么做。

sentences.en: You also get men who are called satires and the satire has a hint of the goat.
sentences.zh: 还有一些被称为萨提尔的男性，萨提尔带有山羊的特征。

sentences.en: Like David Lloyd George.
sentences.zh: 就像大卫·劳埃德·乔治。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, like Lloyd George, it's this kind of the exciting sense that you're casting off the norms and you can do whatever you like.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像劳埃德·乔治一样，这是一种令人兴奋的感觉，仿佛你正在抛弃常规，可以随心所欲。

sentences.en: And mynad's satires, both are following the same
sentences.zh: 迈纳德斯和萨提尔，都在追随同一个

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 神。

sentences.en: And one of the names that this God has is Bacchus for obvious reasons.
sentences.zh: 这个神的名字之一就是巴克科斯，原因显而易见。

sentences.en: He's the God of the
sentences.zh: 他是

sentences.en: Bacchaeia.
sentences.zh: 巴凯亚之神。

sentences.en: He's also known as Omestes, the eater of raw flesh.
sentences.zh: 他也被称为俄梅斯蒂斯，也就是生食血肉者。

sentences.en: He has a whole host of other names.
sentences.zh: 他还有许多其他的名字。

sentences.en: But his original name, the name by which the Greeks generally refer to him, is Dionysus.
sentences.zh: 但他最初的名字，也是希腊人通常称呼他的名字，是狄奥尼索斯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Dionysus.
sentences.zh: 所以就是狄奥尼索斯。

sentences.en: Of all the Greek gods, Tom, I have to say I've always found him the most mysterious.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，在所有的希腊神灵中，我必须说我一直觉得他最神秘。

sentences.en: And obviously he's the most unsettling because of the rites that are associated with him.
sentences.zh: 很显然，由于与他相关的那些仪式，他也是最让人感到不安的。

sentences.en: And we talked in previous episodes about how people generally encounter the Greek myths
sentences.zh: 我们在之前的节目中讨论过，人们通常是在童年时期作为童话故事来接触希腊神话的

sentences.en: when they're children, as children's stories.
sentences.zh: 当他们还是孩子的时候。

sentences.en: But Dionysus doesn't really fit in them at all.
sentences.zh: 但狄奥尼索斯根本不适合出现在这些故事里。

sentences.en: When people think of the Olympians, he's not one of the names that first comes up.
sentences.zh: 当人们想到奥林匹斯山诸神时，他并不是最先浮现的名字之一。

sentences.en: But as we'll see, as I know you're going to talk about, scholars have become more and more interested in Dionysus over the last century or so.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们将要看到的，正如我所知你要谈论的那样，在过去的一个世纪左右里，学者们对狄奥尼索斯的兴趣越来越浓厚。

sentences.en: And he's moved from the periphery really to sort of center stage in historians' understandings of the Greeks and their, and I was about to say their religion.
sentences.zh: 在历史学家对希腊人及其——我本想说他们的宗教——的理解中，他真的从边缘走向了舞台中心。

sentences.en: I know you'll question the word religion and their experience of the supernatural.
sentences.zh: 我知道你会质疑“宗教”这个词，以及他们对超自然现象的体验。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So Dionysus tends not to feature in children's books.
sentences.zh: 所以狄奥尼索斯往往不会出现在儿童读物中。

sentences.en: And also he has always been a challenge to those who have an idea of ancient Greece as, you know, a world of serenity and kind of harmony, light and rationalism and all of that.
sentences.zh: 而且，对于那些把古希腊视为一个充满宁静、和谐、光明、理性等等的世界的人来说，他一直是一个挑战。

sentences.en: And this was a stereotype of ancient Greece that was very popular, particularly in Germany in the 18th and 19th centuries.
sentences.zh: 这是对古希腊的一种刻板印象，在18世纪和19世纪的德国尤为流行。

sentences.en: So enthusiasts for ancient Greece were always kind of mooning over the noble simplicity and quiet grandeur, as one of them put it, of Greek civilization.
sentences.zh: 因此，古希腊的狂热爱好者总是带着怀旧的心情赞叹希腊文明那“高贵的单纯和静穆的伟大”，正如其中一人所说的那样。

sentences.en: But there was a kind of reaction against that bubbling under in
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪的德国，暗地里涌动着一种对这种观点的反弹情绪。

sentences.en: 19th century Germany.
sentences.zh: 19世纪的德国。

sentences.en: And the classicist who most famously reacts against it is the great philosopher
sentences.zh: 对此做出最著名反弹的古典学者是伟大的哲学家

sentences.en: Friedrich Nietzsche, who oddly ends up talking to a horse in a quite kind of Dionysian manner.
sentences.zh: 弗里德里希·尼采，他很奇怪地最终以一种相当狄奥尼索斯式的方式跟一匹马说话。

sentences.en: But very early on in his career, long before that, he published a book called The Birth of
sentences.zh: 但在他职业生涯的早期，在那很久以前，他出版了一本书叫作《悲剧的

sentences.en: Tragedy.
sentences.zh: 诞生》。

sentences.en: And he was only 28 when he did it.
sentences.zh: 他写这本书时年仅28岁。

sentences.en: He was already a professor of Greek.
sentences.zh: 当时他已经是希腊语教授了。

sentences.en: And essentially in that book, he is doing for Dionysus what Freud would do for Oedipus a couple of decades
sentences.zh: 基本上在这本书中，他为狄奥尼索斯所做的事情，就如同弗洛伊德几十年后为俄狄浦斯所做的一样

sentences.en: later, kind of make him into, I guess you'd call him a meme now, something, an expression
sentences.zh: 后来的事情，某种程度上把他变成了一个模因，你现在可能会这么叫他，一种

sentences.en: of something that seems simultaneously very ancient, but kind of thrillingly modern, thrillingly
sentences.zh: 表达某种既显得非常古老，但又极其现代、极其

sentences.en: 19th century.
sentences.zh: 19世纪的事物。

sentences.en: And what Nietzsche is doing in The Birth of Tragedy is to contrast Dionysus with
sentences.zh: 尼采在《悲剧的诞生》中所做的是，将狄奥尼索斯与

sentences.en: Apollo, who for the Greeks is the god of light, of beauty.
sentences.zh: 阿波罗进行对比，阿波罗对希腊人来说是光明之神、美丽之神。

sentences.en: And Nietzsche insists that you can't really understand Greek civilization if you just emphasize the light and the beauty.
sentences.zh: 尼采坚称，如果你只强调光明和美丽，你就无法真正理解希腊文明。

sentences.en: You also have to recognize the deeply Dionysian qualities that Greek civilization had as well.
sentences.zh: 你还必须承认希腊文明中同样具有的深刻的狄奥尼索斯特质。

sentences.en: And, you know, I mean, Nietzsche is more than familiar with the Bacchae.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，尼采对《巴克科斯女祭司》可以说是了如指掌。

sentences.en: The Bacchae plays a key role in The Birth of
sentences.zh: 《巴克科斯女祭司》在《悲剧的

sentences.en: Tragedy.
sentences.zh: 诞生》中扮演了关键角色。

sentences.en: And he, you know, he, you know, all this kind of tearing people to pieces and things.
sentences.zh: 而且他，你知道的，所有这些把人撕成碎片的事情。

sentences.en: He says, he recognizes the darkness.
sentences.zh: 他说，他意识到了黑暗面。

sentences.en: He said, an effusive transgression of the sexual order whose wave swept away all family life and its venerable principles, an abominable mixture of sensuality and cruelty.
sentences.zh: 他说，“对性秩序的肆意践踏，其浪潮席卷了所有的家庭生活及其古老的原则，是感官与残忍的一种令人厌恶的混合。”

sentences.en: So he's saying that's a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他是说这是一件坏事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Not in favor of that.
sentences.zh: 他并不支持这一点。

sentences.en: But then he is also saying that it has, you know, the brilliant size to it.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时他也认为，它具有极其辉煌的一面。

sentences.en: Essentially it's fun, or as he puts it, the blissful rapture which rises up from the innermost depths of men.
sentences.zh: 本质上它很有趣，或者正如他所说，“从人类内心深处升起的极乐狂喜”。

sentences.en: I mean, that is German for fun, basically.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这基本上就是德语里的“有趣”。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 我确信他是用一个词表达的。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 用一个又长又大的德语单词。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The essence of the Dionysian, Nietzsche says, basically it's like, it's, it's like getting drunk.
sentences.zh: 尼采说，狄奥尼索斯精神的本质，基本上就像是，就像是喝醉了。

sentences.en: It's like getting pissed.
sentences.zh: 就像喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: It's intoxication.
sentences.zh: 这就是陶醉。

sentences.zh: 对于希腊人来说，狄奥尼索斯是发明了葡萄酒的神。

sentences.en: So famously Dionysus is the God of, of getting drunk, but he's also the God who is there when humans experience the thrill of nature that has not been tamed by humans.
sentences.zh: 因此，众所周知，狄奥尼索斯是醉酒之神，但他也是当人类体验到未被人类驯服的自然之惊险时在场的神。

sentences.en: So the thrill of the wild.
sentences.zh: 也就是荒野的刺激。

sentences.en: And also, and I think very germanely, and this is part of what Nietzsche found so fascinating
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为非常贴切的是，这也是尼采发现它如此迷人的一部分原因，当然也是20世纪人们发现它迷人的地方，

sentences.en: about it, and it's certainly what people have found fascinating about it in the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 那就是当你把自己的个体意识融入到一个群体中时所获得的狂喜感。

sentences.zh: 到了这个时候，对彭透斯来说，就好像那种飘飘欲仙的感觉开始起效了。

sentences.en: He's getting increasingly spaced out.
sentences.zh: 他的精神状态越来越恍惚。

sentences.en: And he essentially is putty now in Dionysus' hands.
sentences.zh: 而且他现在基本上就是狄奥尼索斯手中的橡皮泥。

sentences.en: He does whatever Dionysus tells him to do.
sentences.zh: 狄奥尼索斯叫他做什么，他就做什么。

sentences.en: And Dionysus persuades Pentheus that what he should really do is go up into the heights and spy on the manads.
sentences.zh: 狄奥尼索斯说服彭透斯，他真正应该做的是去高处窥探迈纳德。

sentences.en: And that the best thing, the best way to do that would be for Pentheus to dress up as a woman, to dress up as a manad.
sentences.zh: 最好的办法、最好的方式就是彭透斯女扮男装，打扮成迈纳德的样子。

sentences.en: I feel like nothing good is going to, well, I know that nothing good is going to happen to Pentheus.
sentences.zh: 我觉得没有什么好事会……好吧，我知道不会有什么好事降临到彭透斯头上。

sentences.en: He's making some bad choices.
sentences.zh: 他做出了一些糟糕的选择。

sentences.en: He is making some, but, you know, then again, he's kind of off his face.
sentences.zh: 他确实做了一些，不过话说回来，他整个人已经神智不清了。

sentences.en: And so Pentheus says, yeah, that's a brilliant idea.
sentences.zh: 于是彭透斯说，好啊，这主意绝了。

sentences.en: And by now he's really tripping.
sentences.zh: 这时候他真的产生幻觉了。

sentences.en: So he says, I seem to see two sons are double Thebes.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，我好像看到了两个太阳，或者说有两个底比斯。

sentences.en: He looks at Dionysus and he sees a pair of horns sprouting from his head.
sentences.zh: 他看着狄奥尼索斯，看到他的头上长出了一对角。

sentences.en: And he is starting to recognize the God for what he is.
sentences.zh: 他开始认出这位神明的真面目了。

sentences.en: So he puts on his, you know, his fawn, fawn skin dress.
sentences.zh: 于是他穿上了他的小鹿皮裙。

sentences.en: And then Dionysus leads him off stage and they're going up to the mountain.
sentences.zh: 然后狄奥尼索斯领着他离开舞台，朝山上走去。

sentences.en: And it doesn't take long for a messenger to appear on the stage and to report what happened next.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，一个信使出现在舞台上，汇报了接下来发生的事。

sentences.en: And we're told that Pentheus had reached the heights of Mount Kitharon.
sentences.zh: 我们得知，彭透斯已经抵达了基思戎山的高处。

sentences.en: And he wants a good view of the manads who are, you know, rampaging around, having their rave, all of that.
sentences.zh: 他想好好看一眼那些四处狂欢、纵情派对的迈纳德。

sentences.en: And so
sentences.zh: 于是

sentences.en: Dionysus pulls down a pine tree and he puts Pentheus on the top of the pine tree.
sentences.zh: 狄奥尼索斯拉弯了一棵松树，把彭透斯放在树顶上。

sentences.en: And then he twang, you know, he lets the pine snap back up so that Pentheus is then at the top of the tree, looking down at the manads.
sentences.zh: 然后松树“啪”地一声弹了回去，这样彭透斯就到了树顶，俯视着下面的迈纳德。

sentences.en: And then Dionysus, the rotter, yells over to the manads and says,
sentences.zh: 接着，这个混蛋狄奥尼索斯朝着迈纳德大喊大叫，说道：

sentences.en: Hey, look at this.
sentences.zh: 嘿，快看这个。

sentences.en: There's a spy pointing up at the hapless Pentheus who's on the top of the tree.
sentences.zh: 有个探子正指着树顶上那个倒霉的彭透斯。

sentences.en: And the manads go absolutely mad and they start shaking the tree.
sentences.zh: 迈纳德们顿时发疯似地开始摇晃树木。

sentences.en: And then the herdsman says, from his high perch, plunging, crashing to the earth, Pentheus fell with one incessant scream as he understood what end was near.
sentences.zh: 然后牧人说，从高高的栖息处坠落，彭透斯伴随着一声凄厉的惨叫摔向地面，因为他明白了最后的结局已经降临。

sentences.en: And that passage that you read at the beginning of this show, that is what happens.
sentences.zh: 而你在节目开头读的那段选段，描述的就是这件事。

sentences.en: He is torn to pieces.
sentences.zh: 他被撕成了碎片。

sentences.en: And shortly afterwards on stage, Agave appears and she's cradling her son's head.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，阿加韦出现在舞台上，手里抱着她儿子的头颅。

sentences.en: And effectively, you know, what the actor must have been holding is the mask of Pentheus.
sentences.zh: 实际上，演员手里拿的肯定是彭透斯的假面。

sentences.en: And presumably Agave is played by the same actor who'd been playing
sentences.zh: 而且大概饰演阿加韦的演员，就是之前饰演

sentences.en: Pentheus.
sentences.zh: 彭透斯的同一个演员。

sentences.en: So Agave thinks that what she's holding is the head of a lion.
sentences.zh: 所以阿加韦以为自己手里拿的是一颗狮子的头。

sentences.en: She thinks that's what she's torn to pieces.
sentences.zh: 她以为那就是她撕碎的东西。

sentences.en: And it's only gradually in obedience to the promptings of Cadmus, her father, that she kind of comes out of her ecstatic state and realizes what it is she's holding and what it
sentences.zh: 只是在她的父亲卡德摩斯的不断提醒下，她才渐渐从狂喜的状态中清醒过来，意识到自己手里拿的究竟是什么，

sentences.en: is that she's done.
sentences.zh: 以及自己做了什么。

sentences.en: She's devastated.
sentences.zh: 她崩溃了。

sentences.en: She and her sisters are sent into exile and Cadmus and his wife are turned into snakes.
sentences.zh: 她和她的姐妹们被流放，卡德摩斯和他的妻子则变成了蛇。

sentences.en: So a bad day for the royal family of Thebes.
sentences.zh: 所以底比斯王室今天过得很糟糕。

sentences.en: And the moral of the story is summed up by Cadmus at the very end of the play.
sentences.zh: 故事的寓意由卡德摩斯在戏剧的最后进行了总结。

sentences.en: If any man derides the unseen world, let him ponder the death of Pentheus and believe in the gods.
sentences.zh: 如果有人嘲笑未知的世界，就让他思考彭透斯的死，并去信仰神明吧。

sentences.en: So a blood-soaked denouement, an absolutely devastating play.
sentences.zh: 这是一个血流成河的结局，一部极具毁灭性的戏剧。

sentences.en: And the obvious question is, what does it mean?
sentences.zh: 显而易见的问题是，这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: What's the point?
sentences.zh: 意义何在？

sentences.en: Because are we to see Pentheus as the villain, as it were, who's being punished for not embracing the spirit of Dionysus?
sentences.zh: 因为我们应该把彭透斯看作是反派吗？也就是因未能拥抱狄奥尼索斯精神而受到惩罚的人？

sentences.en: Or are we, you know, is Pentheus a martyr, a victim?
sentences.zh: 还是说，彭透斯是个烈士、是个受害者？

sentences.en: And should we feel sorry for him?
sentences.zh: 我们应该同情他吗？

sentences.en: And is Dionysus actually a terrible person or terrible god?
sentences.zh: 狄奥尼索斯实际上是一个可怕的人或可怕的神吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I guess that's the point about the green myths, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这就是希腊神话的意义所在，对吧？

sentences.en: That it's impossible to fix a simplistic meaning on something that seems so slippery and so nuanced, but also, frankly, so strange and so terrifying.
sentences.zh: 对于如此多变、细腻，同时也坦率地说如此诡异和可怕的东西，根本无法强加一个简单的解释。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: There are critics.
sentences.zh: 有些评论家。

sentences.en: You see Pentheus as the villain, or Dionysus the villain.
sentences.zh: 你把彭透斯看作反派，或者把狄奥尼索斯看作反派。

sentences.en: You can stage it.
sentences.zh: 你可以这样编排。

sentences.en: I mean, you could stage it as being about the coming of the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以把它排成关于纳粹崛起的剧目。

sentences.en: You could cast
sentences.zh: 你可以把

sentences.en: Dionysus as, you know, as Hitler, or you could stage it with, you know, Pentheus as some boring square who is refusing to drop out and join the hippies.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以把狄奥尼索斯设想成希特勒，或者你也可以这样排演：把彭透斯塑造成一个顽固不化的老古董，拒绝脱离主流去加入嬉皮士。

sentences.en: And as you say, that is a kind of the measure of the richness of this, of Greek myth and of tragedy, is that two and a half thousand years on, it still has this kind of richness.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这正是希腊神话与悲剧丰富底蕴的一种体现——时隔两千五百年，它依然拥有这种丰富的内涵。

sentences.en: It can be interpreted and adapted.
sentences.zh: 它可以被各种解读和改编。

sentences.en: But I'm guessing that that's a very modern way of viewing it, right?
sentences.zh: 但我猜这是一种非常现代的观看视角，对吧？

sentences.en: That the Athenians, when they saw it as part of a communal experience that is a central part of their city's calendar, and you know how important their civic culture is to them.
sentences.zh: 雅典人在观看时，它是作为一种集体体验存在的，这是他们城市日历中的核心部分，而且你知道公民文化对他们有多重要。

sentences.en: They would not have said, oh, this has multiple meanings and it's very slippery and nuanced.
sentences.zh: 他们当时绝不会说：哦，这有多种含义，而且非常含糊微妙。

sentences.en: They would have said, it has one meaning and the meaning is this.
sentences.zh: 他们会说：它只有一个含义，其含义就是这个。

sentences.en: So what is it?
sentences.zh: 那究竟是什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think the context is key.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为背景是关键。

sentences.en: The fact that they are staring down the barrel of total ruin, and they're sitting there watching the dramatic portrayal of a city being utterly destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他们正面临着彻底毁灭的绝境，而他们就坐在那里，看着戏剧中对一座城市彻底毁灭的描绘。

sentences.en: So Euripides is very precise about this in the Bacchae, that the ruin that's visited on Pentheus is also a ruin that is visited on Thebes.
sentences.zh: 因此，欧里庇得斯在《巴克科斯女祭司》中对此非常明确，降临在彭透斯身上的毁灭，同样也是降临在底比斯身上的毁灭。

sentences.en: So to quote Euripides, the city streets tremble in guilt as every Theban repents too late his blindness and his blasphemy.
sentences.zh: 引用欧里庇得斯的话：城市街道在内疚中颤抖，每一个底比斯人都为自己盲目与亵渎而过迟地感到忏悔。

sentences.en: And I think it's impossible to believe that Athenians wouldn't have felt those lines as incredibly chilling and thought about how
sentences.zh: 我想雅典人不可能不为这些台词感到无比脊背发凉，并且会去联想

sentences.en: the ruin that's going to be visited on Thebes is going to, you know, might well be the ruin that's visited on them.
sentences.zh: 即将降临到底比斯的毁灭，你知道的，很可能就是即将降临到他们身上的毁灭。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And what's more, it's the men who are sitting there thinking about it and they're watching
sentences.zh: 而且更重要的是，正是这些男人正坐在那里思考着这些，他们看着

sentences.en: Pentheus, the king who has responsibility for the day-to-day affairs of his city.
sentences.zh: 彭透斯，这个负责城市日常事务的国王。

sentences.en: In a democracy, it's the mass of the male citizens who have that responsibility.
sentences.zh: 在民主制下，承担这一责任的正是广大男性公民。

sentences.en: So they're watching Pentheus lead Thebes to disaster and they must have been reflecting, well, you know, Pentheus is us.
sentences.zh: 所以他们看着彭透斯引领底比斯走向灾难，他们肯定会反思：好吧，你知道的，彭透斯就是我们。

sentences.en: We, the citizen body who have responsibility for the day-to-day running of this city, whether it goes to war, how we conduct that war, we likewise have led our city to ruin.
sentences.zh: 我们这些负责城市日常运作的公民群体，无论是决定是否开战，还是如何进行这场战争，我们同样把自己的城市引向了毁灭。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it must have been devastating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这一定具有毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: But their mistakes, if they are mistakes, have been political, military, diplomatic ones.
sentences.zh: 但他们的错误，如果这也是错误的话，一直是政治、军事和外交上的错误。

sentences.en: Pentheus' mistake is that he doesn't fully embrace what you would call Tom, to do a Tom
sentences.zh: 而彭透斯的错误在于他没有完全拥抱——用汤姆的话来说，来一次“汤姆·霍兰德式”的表达——超自然的维度。

sentences.en: Hollandism, the dimension of the supernatural.
sentences.zh: 霍兰德式的说法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Is Euripides arguing that that is also the Athenians' mistake?
sentences.zh: 欧里庇得斯是在争辩说这也是雅典人的错误吗？

sentences.en: Is he a sort of, is there a slightly Savonarola aspect, Savonarola and Florence aspects of this?
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上，这里面有没有一点萨沃纳罗拉式的色彩，萨沃纳罗拉与佛罗伦萨的色彩？

sentences.en: Basically, you haven't, this is an opportunity for you to revive your gravelly voice, Tom,
sentences.zh: 基本上，你还没有——这是一个让你展现低沉沙哑嗓音的机会，汤姆，

sentences.en: Savonarola's voice.
sentences.zh: 萨沃纳罗拉的声音。

sentences.en: Is he, but is Euripides saying the mistakes, you know, the political mistakes are merely a symptom of a deeper kind of moral, spiritual malaise?
sentences.zh: 他是说，但欧里庇得斯是在说这些错误，你知道的，政治错误仅仅是一种更深层次的道德和精神混乱的症状吗？

sentences.en: Well, as in the Bacchae, so in the dying days of the Great War with Sparta, the Athenians would take for granted that the gods are actors in the drama of what is happening.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如在《巴克科斯女祭司》中一样，在与斯巴达大战的垂死挣扎中，雅典人会理所当然地认为神灵正是正在发生的事情这一戏剧中的演员。

sentences.en: And normally for the Athenians, the readiness of the gods to intervene in the affairs of their city is seen as a positive.
sentences.zh: 通常对雅典人而言，神灵随时准备干涉他们城市的事务被视为一件积极的事。

sentences.en: So to quote Greg Anderson, who I've already cited in this series, in his book, The Realness
sentences.zh: 正如引用我在这系列中已经引述过的格雷格·安德森在他的书《往事之真实》中所说：

sentences.en: of Things PaSt. For the Athenians, the gods of Attica were not some group of faceless superhuman hired contractors.
sentences.zh: 对于雅典人来说，阿提卡的诸神并不是什么面目模糊的超人雇佣承包商。

sentences.en: They were something closer to benevolent governors or caring parents, beings who perpetually monitored and managed the shared local environment, taking a personal
sentences.zh: 他们更像是仁慈的统治者或关爱备至的父母，这些存在不断地监督和管理着共享的本土环境，对他们所挑选的人民的生活和福祉

sentences.en: interest in the life and well-being of their chosen people.
sentences.zh: 倾注了个人般的关切。

sentences.en: And the chosen people is the demos.
sentences.zh: 而这被挑选的人民就是人民大众（demos）。

sentences.en: That is what the democracy is.
sentences.zh: 这就是民主制。

sentences.en: It's the rule of the chosen people of Attica, the chosen people of Athena.
sentences.zh: 它是阿提卡被选民的统治，是雅典娜被选民的统治。

sentences.en: And this notion of the Athenians as a chosen people of Athena and of other gods as well, worshipped by the Athenians.
sentences.zh: 雅典人作为雅典娜以及其他神灵（受雅典人崇拜）的选民这一概念。

sentences.en: This embraces women as well as men.
sentences.zh: 这不仅涵盖了男性，也涵盖了女性。

sentences.en: And in fact, it is women far more than men who are entrusted with the rituals that exist to please the gods and thereby to keep the demos secure.
sentences.zh: 事实上，肩负着取悦神灵从而维护人民大众安全的各种仪式的，远不止男性，更多的是女性。

sentences.en: So that's why these women are going off to the temple of Dionysus in the swamp.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这些女性要前往沼泽中的狄奥尼索斯神庙。

sentences.en: They're the ones who preside over the sacred rituals, but there are other rituals as well.
sentences.zh: 她们是主持这些神圣仪式的人，不过也有其他的仪式。

sentences.en: So from childhood, they've been doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以从童年起，她们就一直在这样做。

sentences.en: So at the age of 10, we're told the girls of Athens go out to a shrine of Artemis, the goddess of the hunt on the shores of
sentences.zh: 因此我们得知，雅典的女孩在10岁时就会前往阿提卡海岸边狩猎女神阿尔忒弥斯的一个神殿。

sentences.en: Attica.
sentences.zh: 阿提卡。

sentences.en: And there they turn into bears and they run with Artemis, or they tend the sacred snake on
sentences.zh: 在那里她们变成母熊并与阿尔忒弥斯一起奔跑，或者她们照看卫城上的神圣灵蛇，

sentences.en: the Acropolis, or they weave robes for Athena, which are carried up onto the Acropolis and are used to adorn her statues.
sentences.zh: 或者她们为雅典娜织造长袍，这些长袍被抬上卫城并用来装点她的雕像。

sentences.en: And Euripides himself is fully conscious of this role that women are mandated to play in securing the health of the demos and of Athens, because we have a fragment from an
sentences.zh: 欧里庇得斯本人也完全意识到了女性在确保人民大众和雅典健康方面被委以重任的这一角色，因为我们保留了一段来自另一部已失传戏剧的片段，他在其中明确阐述了这一点。

sentences.en: otherwise lost play in which he states this explicitly.
sentences.zh: 因此，引述这段残篇：关于与神灵的关系，我认为这是比任何事情都重要的事情，我们女性才扮演着主导角色。

sentences.en: So to quote this fragment, as regards relations with the gods, matters which I judge to be more important than anything, it is we women who have the leading role to play.
sentences.zh: 所以他在这个片段中借女性之口表达观点。

sentences.en: So he's ventriloquizing a woman in this fragment.
sentences.zh: 因为有许多仪式是男性无法合法执行的，但当由女性来主持时便会繁荣昌盛。

sentences.en: For there are many rights which cannot legitimately be performed by men, but which flourish when women conduct them.
sentences.zh: 可以说，凡人与神灵交往中所显现的秩序，是一种女性的秩序。

sentences.en: The order which prevails in the engagements of mortals with the gods is then, it can be said, a female one.
sentences.zh: 既然如此，再次想象一下，当坐在那里明知自己的城市正处于彻底毁灭的边缘，却看到女性发狂般地

sentences.en: And so that being so, again, imagine how terrifying it must have been to sit there knowing that your city is on the brink of total ruin, watching women running amok,
sentences.zh: 以导致国家毁灭的方式崇拜狄奥尼索斯，这该是多么令人恐惧啊。

sentences.en: worshipping Dionysus in a way that causes ruin for the state.
sentences.zh: 在《巴克科斯女祭司》中，女性和男性一样深深卷入了底比斯的崩溃之中。

sentences.en: In the Bacchae, women are embroiled in the collapse of Thebes just as much as men are.

sentences.en: That would make total sense.
sentences.zh: 这完全合乎情理。

sentences.en: They don't actually, if you said to somebody, are you interested in the stories of Usyn Kronos or whatever?
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你随便问一个人，你对尤森·克洛诺斯或其他什么人的故事感兴趣吗？

sentences.en: They'd say, sure, everyone knows these stories.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，当然，谁不知道这些故事啊。

sentences.en: Do you believe them?
sentences.zh: 你相信它们吗？

sentences.en: They'd say, I don't really think about them that much, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，说实话，我其实没怎么想过这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, we, we observe the rituals, of course, but I've got better things to think about.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们当然遵循这些仪式，但我有更重要的事要考虑。

sentences.en: So if we look at Plato, he sets up this, this school outside Athens called the Academy.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们看看柏拉图，他在雅典郊外建立了一所学校，叫做学园。

sentences.en: And it's so influential that in the long run, you know, it gives us the word academic, but it's worth emphasizing.
sentences.zh: 它影响深远，从长远来看，你知道的，给我们留下了“学术”这个词，但值得强调的是。

sentences.en: It stands outside Athens.
sentences.zh: 它座落在雅典城外。

sentences.en: It's not in the city and it is named after the tomb of a hero, Academus.
sentences.zh: 它不在城内，而是以一位英雄阿卡德摩斯的陵墓命名的。

sentences.en: So the presence of, of, of, of myth is there right in the heart of Plato's school.
sentences.zh: 因此，神话的存在就位于柏拉图学园的核心。

sentences.en: And it, you know, this, the Academy cannot remotely compare for kind of splendor and cost and prestige with the temples that continue to stand in
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这个学园在宏伟程度、造价和声望上，根本无法与雅典那些依然屹立的

sentences.en: Athens.
sentences.zh: 神庙相提并论。

sentences.en: No one is going to say, oh, the Academy is more important than the Parthenon.
sentences.zh: 没有人会说，哦，学园比帕台农神庙还要重要。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's the equivalent of a, I don't know, a liberal arts college in upstate New
sentences.zh: 所以这相当于，我不知道，纽约州北部的一所文理

sentences.en: York, where they're coming up with all kinds of wacky theories and whatnot, and they're living outside capitalism, but actually in New York city, no one cares.
sentences.zh: 学院，他们在那里构思各种古怪的理论之类，过着脱离资本主义的生活，但实际上在纽约市根本没人关心。

sentences.en: And they're just, you know, kind of, yes, I suppose kind of, but the other thing to emphasize is that philosophy doesn't banish myth.
sentences.zh: 而他们只是，你知道的，差不多吧——是的，我想某种程度上是这样的，但另一件需要强调的是，哲学并没有驱逐神话。

sentences.en: It just creates a new one.
sentences.zh: 它只是创造了一个新的神话。

sentences.en: So Xenophanes, even as he's saying, you know, cows would, would worship cows.
sentences.zh: 因此色诺芬，尽管他在说，你知道的，牛也会崇拜牛。

sentences.en: What he's really disputing is the fact that the gods look like humans.
sentences.zh: 他真正质疑的其实是神长得像人这一事实。

sentences.en: He absolutely believes in a God.
sentences.zh: 他绝对相信有一位神。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, and it sounds very much, you know, it will sound familiar to, to Monotheus today.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来非常，你知道的，对今天的一神论者来说会觉得很熟悉。

sentences.en: Xenophanes wrote, there is one God greatest among gods and men, similar to mortals, neither in shape nor in thought.
sentences.zh: 色诺芬写道：神只有一位，在神明和人类中是最伟大的，无论在形体上还是在思想上，都与凡人截然不同。

sentences.en: And those who are arguing that, you know, the cosmos is made of air or fire or moisture or whatever.
sentences.zh: 而那些争论说，你知道的，宇宙是由空气、火、水分或其他什么构成的人。

sentences.en: The assumption is, is that these elements are themselves divine.
sentences.zh: 他们的假设是，这些元素本身就是神圣的。

sentences.en: So in that sense, the whole cosmos is divine and Plato is himself the greatest of all myth makers.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，整个宇宙都是神圣的，而柏拉图本人就是所有神话制造者中最伟大的一个。

sentences.en: And what he does with momentous consequences for the way that we continue to think today is that he makes the real unreal and the unreal real, because
sentences.zh: 他对我们今天的思维方式产生了深远的影响，他把真实的变成虚幻的，把虚幻的变成真实的，因为

sentences.en: what he's arguing is that beyond the world, as we perceive it, there is another world, which is perfect, immortal, unchangeable.
sentences.zh: 他所争论的是，在我们感知的世界之外，还有另一个世界，那是完美、永恒且不变的。

sentences.en: And the way that this is always summed up is that there are, you know, you have tables, all kinds of tables, but these are merely reflections
sentences.zh: 总结这种观点的经典说法是，你有各种各样的桌子，形形色色的桌子，但这些都只是

sentences.en: of the perfect table that kind of exists as in an ideal state.
sentences.zh: 以理想状态存在的完美桌子的倒影。

sentences.en: So what Plato is doing, he's banishing the Homeric gods, but he's enshrining new gods.
sentences.zh: 所以柏拉图在做的，是驱逐了荷马诸神，但他供奉了新的神明。

sentences.en: And these are kind of essentially abstract nouns, you know, kind of the just, the beautiful, the good, whatever.
sentences.zh: 这些基本上都是些抽象名词，你知道的，正义、美好、良善等等。

sentences.en: And rather than a pachea, so going out and celebrating on the mountain, what Plato is offering his followers
sentences.zh: 柏拉图向追随者提供的不是帕查亚节那种走到山上去庆祝的狂欢

sentences.en: is an ascent, the idea that the individual has an ideal form, namely, you know, in the form of a soul or whatever you want to call it.
sentences.zh: 而是一种精神的升华，也就是认为个体拥有一个理想形态，也就是，你知道的，灵魂的形式或随便你怎么称呼它。

sentences.en: And that the soul can ascend from the dimension of the material to, as Plato puts it, the best of everything, which can be comprehended by thought and which is eternal.
sentences.zh: 并且灵魂可以从物质维度升华到——正如柏拉图所说——世间至美之境，它能被思想所理解且永恒不朽。

sentences.en: And this in effect is God.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是上帝。

sentences.en: And this concept is going to be a massive influence on
sentences.zh: 这个概念将对

sentences.en: Christianity, on Islam.
sentences.zh: 基督教和伊斯兰教产生巨大影响。

sentences.en: And so to quote Walter Burkhart in his great book on Greek religion, since Plato, there has been no theology, which has not stood in his shadow.
sentences.zh: 借用沃尔特·布克哈特在他那本关于希腊宗教的伟大著作中的话：自柏拉图以来，还没有哪一种神学不笼罩在他的阴影之下。

sentences.en: So there's a sense in which the Greek reaction against myth that Plato exemplifies, but you also have Aristotle and other philosophers too.
sentences.zh: 所以某种程度上，柏拉图所体现的希腊人对神话的反弹，虽然亚里士多德和其他哲学家也有份。

sentences.en: This is, this is part of the great river, which will feed into the emergence of Christianity and, and, and, and Islam.
sentences.zh: 这正是汇入基督教和伊斯兰教兴起之中的长河的一部分。

sentences.en: And therefore is of titanic significance, I think.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为这具有极其重大的意义。

sentences.en: So now with Plato and with his ideas, we are heading towards, we're not quite there yet,
sentences.zh: 所以现在随着柏拉图及其思想的出现，我们正朝着——虽然还没完全走到那一步，

sentences.en: but we're heading towards the Hellenistic era, the age associated with Alexander the Great and his successors.
sentences.zh: 但我们正在走向希腊化时代，一个与亚历山大大帝及其继任者紧密相连的时代。

sentences.en: And I guess the obvious question is after Plato and after the, you know, the, the massive political disruption of the emergence of Macedon and Alexander and his empire, what does
sentences.zh: 我想显而易见的问题是，在柏拉图之后，在马其顿、亚历山大及其帝国的崛起带来巨大的政治动荡之后，

sentences.en: this mean for Greek mythology and the Greek stories of the gods?
sentences.zh: 这对希腊神话和希腊诸神的故事意味着什么？

sentences.en: And how does Alexander in particular, how does he come to it?
sentences.zh: 亚历山大本人又是如何看待这一切的？

sentences.en: Because he assumes such massive existential significance.
sentences.zh: 因为他具有如此巨大的存在主义意义。

sentences.en: How does he change the way that Greeks think about the relation between mortal and the immortal?
sentences.zh: 他如何改变了希腊人对凡人与不朽之间关系的看法？

sentences.en: And Tom, this takes us to one of my favorite Greek myths, which is the story of Jason and the Argonauts, the quest for the golden fleece.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这把我们带到了我最喜欢的希腊神话之一，也就是伊阿宋与阿尔戈英雄寻金羊毛的故事。

sentences.zh: 这就是我们下期要讲的内容，对吧？

sentences.zh: 令人兴奋的是，我们其实拥有自己的船员。
